hosting.//: The admin panel, served at the ROOT of its own origin. It used to be planned as odoapp.in/admin; a subdomain keeps it off the marketing site's certificate, its cookies and its analytics, and means a mistake in one config cannot take the other down.
hosting.//redirects: /admin was the old path when this was going to live under the marketing site. Kept as a redirect so a link somebody saved still lands.
hosting.//headers: Sources must not overlap. The CSP names one Supabase project, never both: a policy listing the pair would let a build configured for the wrong environment reach it silently.

headers.value: default-src 'none'; script-src 'self' 'wasm-unsafe-eval'; connect-src 'self' https://identitytoolkit.googleapis.com https://securetoken.googleapis.com https://gezicmstbgfpwwohiboq.supabase.co; img-src 'self' data: https://gezicmstbgfpwwohiboq.supabase.co; style-src 'unsafe-inline'; font-src 'self' data:; worker-src 'self' blob:; base-uri 'self'; form-action 'none'; frame-ancestors 'none'

headers.//: Content-hashed, so the name IS the version — `6e23e54….wasm` cannot ever hold different bytes. `immutable` tells the browser not even to revalidate, which removes a round trip per file on every visit after the first. These two files are 3.5 MB of the 3.6 MB a cold load costs.

A stable filename, so it must revalidate: a cached bundle can reference hashed .wasm files that no longer exist, which is a blank page with a 404 in the console. Revalidation is cheap — it answers 304 with no body.
The entry point. Firebase's hour would make a deploy invisible for an hour to anyone who had already visited.
cleanUrls serves index.html here, and it needs the same treatment.

The string table. A stable name and only 7 KB, so it revalidates rather than being pinned — every label in the app comes out of this file, and serving a stale one after a copy change is worse than one conditional request.

hosting.//cache:
Cache-Control, split by whether a filename can be trusted.
Firebase's default is max-age=3600 on everything, which is wrong in both directions: too short for a content-hashed file that can never change, and too long for an entry point that has to reflect a deploy.
